newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa chalks up gains as origins back away.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa chalks up gains as origins back away.

text.p: London cocoa futures made gains on Friday as origin offers dried up but trade and industry buying bumped in to resistance at the close, traders said.

They thought it was too early to call the market's protracted downtrend over yet. Lack of producer selling after a flood of offers earlier this week enabled the market to head higher at the start, securing a further boost after a positive New York session.
But traders noted speculative selling in late session which boded well with analysts' convictions that overhead supply will keep a lid on prices in the short-term.
"We had an impressive start today. There was reasonable manufacturer buying and no pre-hedge type selling," said one.
But industry was merely "sniffing around" and there is still no sign of a major offtake while the fundamental supply picture remains uncertain.
Sterling's retreat from highs provided arbitrage interest against the dollar-based New York, traders said.
Benchmark March cocoa position initially pierced 880 resistance and rallied to a session high of 886 but failed to sustain its position, finishing at 879 stg a tonne, up seven.
May was also up seven at 899.
Volume totalled 7,129 lots including 1,000 lots of March AAs.
Physical differentials picked up on trade short covering this week. One Ivory Coast afloat traded at 32 stg under LIFFE March after hovering at 55 stg under just before Christmas.
One trader said demand stemmed from physical cocoa being diverted to the United States from Europe to cash in the arbitrage differential.
On the charts, March has will face resistance at Friday's high of 886 stg followed by 895 and 905. Support is well established at 865 for the time being.
